commit_message:
[Torch] Convert integral float zero points of PT2E and torchao ops (#25136)

Converts integer-valued float zero points of PT2E and torchao ops to i32
so they lower to LinalgExt. The constant zero-point check moves from the
`dequantize_affine` verifier into the Torch conversion, which declines
constant zero points outside the quantization bounds.

Part of #24862.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Add target-aware layout materialization

Dispatch-time data tiling assigns layouts inside dispatches, so the
phases before dispatch creation cannot see or propagate them.
Materializing the layouts during global optimization makes that phase
target aware on purpose: layouts propagate through the surrounding
tensor graph, and the packed contractions still fuse with their
epilogues and result unpacks.

Add the experimental --iree-opt-experimental-early-data-tiling flag. It
takes precedence over the other data-tiling placement flags, so
conflicting data-tiling flags are not an error when it is set, and the
route uses the operation families and encoding strategy of
dispatch-time data tiling.

The route applies to modules with a single llvm-cpu target on x86_64 or
AArch64 that uses the CPU encoding resolver without inner-tiled layouts,
and only with the default encoding strategy. For these modules, global
optimization propagates reshapes, normalizes contraction dimensions,
assigns and propagates encodings, and materializes them on the host. It
then records the target on the module, even if nothing was data-tiled.
Dispatch creation therefore skips encoding assignment for the whole
module, always fuses data-tiled ops with their epilogues and result
unpacks, and keeps the loop order of data-tiled convolutions. Other
modules keep dispatch-time data tiling. The enable_inner_tiled check
moves from the CPU encoding models to the Codegen utilities, so that the
eligibility check can share it.

On an Apple M3 Max (local-task, f32, median of 10), the route is within
noise of dispatch-time data tiling for a matmul with bias and ReLU, a
batch matmul with ReLU and a convolution with ReLU. x86_64 has not been
measured.

The optimization options reference documents the route, its limits and
the flag precedence.

The layout decision is split over several passes, supports one CPU
target per module, and adds HAL and Codegen dependencies to the global
phases. The TODOs describe moving it into its own component that decides
per affinity.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: pkgci_summary / summary

  formation. The compiled modules are byte-identical.
- Document in the PropagateAffineQuantization description that pads are
  not moved onto sub-byte storage.

commit_message:
[Build][AMDGPU] Use bitcode from the official ROCM distribution (#25133)

With the sunset of the old artifacts from
`shark-infra/amdgpu-device-libs`, migrate to LLVM bitcode blobs from the
official distribution. The version shall be pinned in
`build_tools/third_party/amdgpu_device_libs/rocm_package.json`.

This increases the bitcode download to 146Mb (in comparison, the WASI
SDK weighs in at <120Mb). Considering we're only using less than 1Mb,
that's unfortunate, but at the moment it's the only way to use the
official maintained source.

Fixes #25131.

Assisted-by: Codex

The v3.13.1 patch release contains a runtime-only VM bytecode verifier repair. Keep the compiler at 3.13.0 and advance the runtime package so the one-shot release workflow publishes only the affected product at a new version.

Signed-off-by: Ben Vanik <ben.vanik@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[Codegen] fix  `fuseConsumersIntoForall` stale op result on worklist (#25189)

`fuseConsumersIntoForall` kept a `SmallDenseSet<OpResult>` of visited
loop results for the whole fusion loop. Every successful
`scf::tileAndFuseConsumer`, however, rebuilds the `scf.forall` with
additional results and erases the old loop, so after the first fusion
the set holds handles of erased ops. `OpResult` equality is pointer
equality: if the allocator later places a new loop where an erased one
was, a result of the new loop compares equal to a stale entry, is
skipped as already visited, and its consumers are never collected.
Nothing fails; the consumer is just left outside the loop.

This is the `windows_x64_msvc` failure in
`Codegen/LLVMCPU/test/tile_and_fuse_producer_consumer_anchoring_root_op.mlir`
(`@scalable_mmt4d_generic_unpack_pack`, e.g.
https://github.com/iree-org/iree/actions/runs/41050722968 on `main`):
mmt4d, generic and unpack are fused, the `linalg.pack` stays outside the
loop.

**Why only Windows?** The new loop is always larger than the one it
replaces (more results and init operands). glibc's malloc is
deterministic and does not serve a larger request from a smaller freed
chunk, so on Linux the same binary and input always place the new loop
elsewhere. The Windows heap behaves differently: its low-fragmentation
layer serves allocations from size buckets of coarse granularity and
selects free blocks with randomization (an exploit mitigation since
Windows 8), so the block freed for an earlier loop is handed to a new
one only occasionally.

The fix keeps no handle to the loop or its results across fusions: the
visited-result set is gone, and the worklist only holds the consumer
ops, which survive every rebuild and are deduplicated by identity. It is
still filled incrementally, from the users of the tiled ops'
`tensor.parallel_insert_slice`s and, after each fusion, of the newly
added loop result.

I couldn't think of any deterministic regression test for this, the
failure needs an address collision dependent on allocator behavior.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

---------

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[Codegen] fix  `fuseConsumersIntoForall` stale op result on worklist (#25189)

`fuseConsumersIntoForall` kept a `SmallDenseSet<OpResult>` of visited
loop results for the whole fusion loop. Every successful
`scf::tileAndFuseConsumer`, however, rebuilds the `scf.forall` with
additional results and erases the old loop, so after the first fusion
the set holds handles of erased ops. `OpResult` equality is pointer
equality: if the allocator later places a new loop where an erased one
was, a result of the new loop compares equal to a stale entry, is
skipped as already visited, and its consumers are never collected.
Nothing fails; the consumer is just left outside the loop.

This is the `windows_x64_msvc` failure in
`Codegen/LLVMCPU/test/tile_and_fuse_producer_consumer_anchoring_root_op.mlir`
(`@scalable_mmt4d_generic_unpack_pack`, e.g.
https://github.com/iree-org/iree/actions/runs/41050722968 on `main`):
mmt4d, generic and unpack are fused, the `linalg.pack` stays outside the
loop.

**Why only Windows?** The new loop is always larger than the one it
replaces (more results and init operands). glibc's malloc is
deterministic and does not serve a larger request from a smaller freed
chunk, so on Linux the same binary and input always place the new loop
elsewhere. The Windows heap behaves differently: its low-fragmentation
layer serves allocations from size buckets of coarse granularity and
selects free blocks with randomization (an exploit mitigation since
Windows 8), so the block freed for an earlier loop is handed to a new
one only occasionally.

The fix keeps no handle to the loop or its results across fusions: the
visited-result set is gone, and the worklist only holds the consumer
ops, which survive every rebuild and are deduplicated by identity. It is
still filled incrementally, from the users of the tiled ops'
`tensor.parallel_insert_slice`s and, after each fusion, of the newly
added loop result.

I couldn't think of any deterministic regression test for this, the
failure needs an address collision dependent on allocator behavior.

commit_message:
[Stream] Keep aliased-loop-results e2e test under the arm64 stack limit

The regression test added in #24841 ends with a gather from an
uninitialized `tensor.empty() : tensor<4420x6xi8>`. Inside the dispatch
that tensor becomes a 26,520-byte stack allocation. On aarch64 the
6-wide inner dimension is split into vector<4> and vector<2> parts, each
with its own copy of the allocation, so the dispatch fails to compile:

  error: 'func.func' op exceeded stack allocation limit of 32768 bytes
  for function. Got 53120 bytes

This has broken the scheduled linux_arm64_clang job since #24841 landed
(the job does not run on PRs).

The gather only reads undefined data and plays no part in the ARC bug
the test covers, so replace it with an elementwise truncation of the
loop result, which is still consumed after the loop. The test now
compiles for aarch64, still fails with "transient buffer has not been
committed" on a compiler from before #24841, and passes on current main.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Stream] Keep aliased-loop-results e2e test under the arm64 stack limit

The regression test added in #24841 ends with a gather from an
uninitialized `tensor.empty() : tensor<4420x6xi8>`. Inside the dispatch
that tensor becomes a 26,520-byte stack allocation. On aarch64 the
6-wide inner dimension is split into vector<4> and vector<2> parts, each
with its own copy of the allocation, so the dispatch fails to compile:

  error: 'func.func' op exceeded stack allocation limit of 32768 bytes
  for function. Got 53120 bytes

This has broken the scheduled linux_arm64_clang job since #24841 landed
(the job does not run on PRs).

The gather only reads undefined data and plays no part in the ARC bug
the test covers, so replace it with an elementwise truncation of the
loop result, which is still consumed after the loop. The test now
compiles for aarch64, still fails with "transient buffer has not been
committed" on a compiler from before #24841, and passes on current main.

[Stream] Keep aliased-loop-results e2e test under the arm64 stack limit

The regression test added in #24841 ends with a gather from an
uninitialized `tensor.empty() : tensor<4420x6xi8>`. Inside the dispatch
that tensor becomes a 26,520-byte stack allocation. On aarch64 the
6-wide inner dimension is split into vector<4> and vector<2> parts, each
with its own copy of the allocation, so the dispatch fails to compile:

  error: 'func.func' op exceeded stack allocation limit of 32768 bytes
  for function. Got 53120 bytes

This has broken the scheduled linux_arm64_clang job since #24841 landed
(the job does not run on PRs).

The gather only reads undefined data and plays no part in the ARC bug
the test covers, so replace it with an elementwise truncation of the
loop result, which is still consumed after the loop. The test now
compiles for aarch64, still fails with "transient buffer has not been
committed" on a compiler from before #24841, and passes on current main.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[CI] Restrict workflow token permissions to read-only

Adds a top-level `permissions: contents: read` to the 28 workflows that
declared no permissions, and drops the top-level `contents: write` and
`pull-requests: write` from clang_tidy.yml (cpp-linter runs with
thread-comments disabled and only needs to read the PR diff).

Jobs that call the GitHub API with the workflow token declare the read
scope they use at job level:
- `pull-requests: read` for the PR diff in clang_tidy.yml and the PR
  description in setup.yml.
- `actions: read` for the cross-workflow artifact download in
  clang_tidy.yml, the run lookup in get_latest_green.sh, and
  `setup_venv.py --fetch-gh-workflow` in the pkgci test workflows.
A called workflow can't exceed its caller's permissions, so the calling
jobs in ci.yml and pkgci.yml grant the same scopes.

Two API failures that used to pass silently now fail the job:
clang_tidy.yml skips clang-tidy only when GitHub rejects the diff as too
large (HTTP 406 `too_large`), and get_latest_green.sh aborts on a failed
`gh api` call instead of counting it as "no green run" and walking the
whole history.

Every write in the release and website workflows still goes through the
`WRITE_ACCESS_TOKEN` PAT. Checkouts that use the PAT now set
`persist-credentials: false`, so the token no longer sits in
`.git/config` while pip and other dependencies are installed. The two
steps that relied on the persisted credential (the candidate tag push
and `mkdocs gh-deploy`) pass the token explicitly instead.

This takes the OpenSSF Scorecard Token-Permissions check from 0 to 10.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[CI] Attest build provenance of rc assets (#25202)

Release assets uploaded by `build_package.yml` are not signed, so users
cannot check that a wheel or `iree-dist` tarball was built by IREE's
release workflow. This adds an [artifact
attestation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/use-artifact-attestations/use-artifact-attestations)
step that signs build provenance for every file uploaded as a release
asset (`./bindist/iree*.*`), right before the upload. Attestations are
signed with Sigstore and stored by GitHub.

Users can verify a downloaded asset with:

```sh
gh attestation verify iree_base_runtime-<version>-<tags>.whl \
  --repo iree-org/iree \
  --signer-workflow iree-org/iree/.github/workflows/build_package.yml
```

The `build_packages` job now declares its token permissions: `id-token`,
`attestations` and `artifact-metadata` for `actions/attest`, plus
`contents: read` for checkout. The release upload is unaffected because
it uses `WRITE_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

This only covers the nightly candidate releases on GitHub releases. It
does not cover stable wheels on PyPI.

commit_message:
[CI] Attest build provenance of rc assets (#25202)

Release assets uploaded by `build_package.yml` are not signed, so users
cannot check that a wheel or `iree-dist` tarball was built by IREE's
release workflow. This adds an [artifact
attestation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/use-artifact-attestations/use-artifact-attestations)
step that signs build provenance for every file uploaded as a release
asset (`./bindist/iree*.*`), right before the upload. Attestations are
signed with Sigstore and stored by GitHub.

Users can verify a downloaded asset with:

```sh
gh attestation verify iree_base_runtime-<version>-<tags>.whl \
  --repo iree-org/iree \
  --signer-workflow iree-org/iree/.github/workflows/build_package.yml
```

The `build_packages` job now declares its token permissions: `id-token`,
`attestations` and `artifact-metadata` for `actions/attest`, plus
`contents: read` for checkout. The release upload is unaffected because
it uses `WRITE_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

This only covers the nightly candidate releases on GitHub releases. It
does not cover stable wheels on PyPI.

commit_message:
[Encoding] Replace packed_storage special cases with interface queries (#25089)

Replaced the explicit `PackedStorageAttr` checks in type propagation,
HAL-to-Stream conversion, and dispatch dimension collapsing with queries
using `SerializableAttr` interface. This will allow other encodings to
use those behaviors without adding any encoding specific checking to
those passes.

Added the three capabilities which describe whether an encoding can be
dropped after storage element-type legalization, skip buffer-view
metadata assertions or remain unchanged during dimensions collapsing.
All the three interface methods default to false. `PackedStorageAttr`
overrides each to return true, preserving the existing behaviour.

Added unit and regression coverage for the added new interface queries
and affected passes. The existing packed-i1 attention and subbyte CPU
end-to-end tests also pass.

Fixes #23306

commit_message:
[CI] Use the workflow token instead of a PAT in release workflows

Replaces every use of the `WRITE_ACCESS_TOKEN` personal access token
with `github.token`, scoped per job:

- tag_release (scheduled and one-shot): `contents: write` to push the
  candidate tag and create the draft release, `actions: write` to
  dispatch Build Release Packages.
- build_packages: `contents: write` to upload release assets.
- validate_and_publish / publish_release: `actions: write` to dispatch
  the next workflow, `contents: write` to publish the release and push
  latest-snapshot.
- validate_packages: `actions: read` to download the build artifacts.
- publish_website: `contents: write` to push gh-pages.

`workflow_dispatch` is exempt from the rule that events caused by the
workflow token do not start workflow runs, so the dispatch chain keeps
working. Publishing a release is not exempt, so the publish job now
dispatches publish_website.yml explicitly for non-candidate releases,
mirroring the condition that workflow applies to the `release` event.

The workflow token is minted per job, scoped to this repository, and
expires with the job, so no long-lived credential remains in the
release pipeline.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[CI] Use the workflow token instead of a PAT in release workflows

Replaces every use of the `WRITE_ACCESS_TOKEN` personal access token
with `github.token`, scoped per job:

- tag_release (scheduled and one-shot): `contents: write` to push the
  candidate tag and create the draft release, `actions: write` to
  dispatch Build Release Packages.
- build_packages: `contents: write` to upload release assets.
- validate_and_publish / publish_release: `actions: write` to dispatch
  the next workflow, `contents: write` to publish the release and push
  latest-snapshot.
- validate_packages: `actions: read` to download the build artifacts.
- publish_website: `contents: write` to push gh-pages.

`workflow_dispatch` is exempt from the rule that events caused by the
workflow token do not start workflow runs, so the dispatch chain keeps
working. Publishing a release is not exempt, so the publish job now
dispatches publish_website.yml explicitly for non-candidate releases,
mirroring the condition that workflow applies to the `release` event.

The workflow token is minted per job, scoped to this repository, and
expires with the job, so no long-lived credential remains in the
release pipeline.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[CI] Restrict workflow token permissions to read-only

Adds a top-level `permissions: contents: read` to the 28 workflows that
declared no permissions, and drops the top-level `contents: write` and
`pull-requests: write` from clang_tidy.yml (cpp-linter runs with
thread-comments disabled and only needs to read the PR diff).

The release and website workflows are unaffected: every write there goes
through the `WRITE_ACCESS_TOKEN` PAT, and read-only API calls work on a
public repository without extra scopes.

Checkouts that use the PAT now set `persist-credentials: false`, so the
token no longer sits in `.git/config` while pip and other dependencies
are installed. The two steps that relied on the persisted credential
(the candidate tag push and `mkdocs gh-deploy`) pass the token
explicitly instead.

This takes the OpenSSF Scorecard Token-Permissions check from 0 to 10.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[CI] Use the workflow token instead of a PAT in release workflows

Replaces every use of the `WRITE_ACCESS_TOKEN` personal access token
with `github.token`, scoped per job:

- tag_release (scheduled and one-shot): `contents: write` to push the
  candidate tag and create the draft release, `actions: write` to
  dispatch Build Release Packages.
- build_packages: `contents: write` to upload release assets.
- validate_and_publish / publish_release: `actions: write` to dispatch
  the next workflow, `contents: write` to publish the release and push
  latest-snapshot.
- validate_packages: `actions: read` to download the build artifacts.
- publish_website: `contents: write` to push gh-pages.

`workflow_dispatch` is exempt from the rule that events caused by the
workflow token do not start workflow runs, so the dispatch chain keeps
working. Publishing a release is not exempt, so the publish job now
dispatches publish_website.yml explicitly for non-candidate releases,
mirroring the condition that workflow applies to the `release` event.

The workflow token is minted per job, scoped to this repository, and
expires with the job, so no long-lived credential remains in the
release pipeline.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert integral float zero points of PT2E and torchao ops (#25136)

Converts integer-valued float zero points of PT2E and torchao ops to i32
so they lower to LinalgExt. The constant zero-point check moves from the
`dequantize_affine` verifier into the Torch conversion, which declines
constant zero points outside the quantization bounds.

Part of #24862.

commit_message:
[CI] Restrict workflow token permissions to read-only

Adds a top-level `permissions: contents: read` to the 28 workflows that
declared no permissions, and drops the top-level `contents: write` and
`pull-requests: write` from clang_tidy.yml (cpp-linter runs with
thread-comments disabled and only needs to read the PR diff).

Jobs that call the GitHub API with the workflow token declare the read
scope they use at job level:
- `pull-requests: read` for the PR diff in clang_tidy.yml and the PR
  description in setup.yml.
- `actions: read` for the cross-workflow artifact download in
  clang_tidy.yml, the run lookup in get_latest_green.sh, and
  `setup_venv.py --fetch-gh-workflow` in the pkgci test workflows.
A called workflow can't exceed its caller's permissions, so the calling
jobs in ci.yml and pkgci.yml grant the same scopes.

Two API failures that used to pass silently now fail the job:
clang_tidy.yml skips clang-tidy only when GitHub rejects the diff as too
large (HTTP 406 `too_large`), and get_latest_green.sh aborts on a failed
`gh api` call instead of counting it as "no green run" and walking the
whole history.

Every write in the release and website workflows still goes through the
`WRITE_ACCESS_TOKEN` PAT. Checkouts that use the PAT now set
`persist-credentials: false`, so the token no longer sits in
`.git/config` while pip and other dependencies are installed. The two
steps that relied on the persisted credential (the candidate tag push
and `mkdocs gh-deploy`) pass the token explicitly instead.

This takes the OpenSSF Scorecard Token-Permissions check from 0 to 10.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[CI] Restrict workflow token permissions to read-only

Adds a top-level `permissions: contents: read` to the 28 workflows that
declared no permissions, and drops the top-level `contents: write` and
`pull-requests: write` from clang_tidy.yml (cpp-linter runs with
thread-comments disabled and only needs to read the PR diff).

Jobs that call the GitHub API with the workflow token declare the read
scope they use at job level:
- `pull-requests: read` for the PR diff in clang_tidy.yml and the PR
  description in setup.yml.
- `actions: read` for the cross-workflow artifact download in
  clang_tidy.yml, the run lookup in get_latest_green.sh, and
  `setup_venv.py --fetch-gh-workflow` in the pkgci test workflows.
A called workflow can't exceed its caller's permissions, so the calling
jobs in ci.yml and pkgci.yml grant the same scopes.

Two API failures that used to pass silently now fail the job:
clang_tidy.yml skips clang-tidy only when GitHub rejects the diff as too
large (HTTP 406 `too_large`), and get_latest_green.sh aborts on a failed
`gh api` call instead of counting it as "no green run" and walking the
whole history.

Every write in the release and website workflows still goes through the
`WRITE_ACCESS_TOKEN` PAT. Checkouts that use the PAT now set
`persist-credentials: false`, so the token no longer sits in
`.git/config` while pip and other dependencies are installed. The two
steps that relied on the persisted credential (the candidate tag push
and `mkdocs gh-deploy`) pass the token explicitly instead.

This takes the OpenSSF Scorecard Token-Permissions check from 0 to 10.

commit_message:
[Build][AMDGPU] Use bitcode from the official ROCM distribution (#25133)

With the sunset of the old artifacts from
`shark-infra/amdgpu-device-libs`, migrate to LLVM bitcode blobs from the
official distribution. The version shall be pinned in
`build_tools/third_party/amdgpu_device_libs/rocm_package.json`.

This increases the bitcode download to 146Mb (in comparison, the WASI
SDK weighs in at <120Mb). Considering we're only using less than 1Mb,
that's unfortunate, but at the moment it's the only way to use the
official maintained source.

Fixes #25131.
